edges.description: Amplified MYCN raises TERT transcription, which makes MYCN amplification a route to telomerase activation rather than a separate telomere maintenance mechanism. TERT expression was higher in MYCN-amplified tumours, and in a MYCN-amplified cell line TERT was the gene most strongly downregulated when MYCN was knocked down. Not every MYCN-amplified tumour takes this route: some express TERT as low as ALT tumours do, and forced MYCN overexpression did not induce TERT where the promoter was repressed.
intermediate_mechanisms: Increased TERT transcription driven by amplified MYCN

edges.description: Constitutive ALK kinase signalling converges on the same proliferative output as MYCN amplification and co-operates with it; ALK-mutant and MYCN-amplified disease frequently co-occur and jointly enhance malignancy.

Telomerase keeps telomeres from eroding, so tumour cells can go on dividing. High-risk neuroblastoma cell lines with neither telomerase activity nor ALT showed continuous telomere shortening, and most lost viability in culture.

Loss of ATRX/DAXX complex function permits alternative lengthening of telomeres. ATRX mutation is associated with loss of nuclear ATRX protein and with ALT, and in one series every ALT tumour carried an ATRX or DAXX alteration. Without ATRX, histone H3.3 is not efficiently deposited at telomeric repeats, replication forks stall there, and the telomeres undergo the homologous recombination that leads to ALT.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of ATRX/DAXX-dependent deposition of histone H3.3 at telomeric repeats

edges.description: ALT maintains telomere length without telomerase, giving the tumour cells that use it an unlimited replicative capacity. High-risk neuroblastoma cell lines with neither ALT nor telomerase activity showed continuous telomere shortening, and most lost viability in culture.

Supplies a molecular switch for the arrest this node asserts: multi-site phosphorylation of Ascl1 converts it from a driver of sympathoadrenal differentiation into an inert factor, matching the phospho-state Ascl1 is held in within neuroblastoma cells.
edges.limitations: Frog AVNA cells are a developmental counterpart of the presumed cell of origin, not tumour cells, and the model contains no transformed tissue — arrest is scored as failure to differentiate on schedule rather than as tumour formation. The link to human disease rests on the observed phospho-state of ASCL1 in neuroblastoma lines, so the model shows the state is sufficient to block differentiation, not that it is what maintains any patient's tumour.
edges.source: Xenopus anteroventral noradrenergic (AVNA) cell differentiation model

edges.description: Positions MYCN upstream of the differentiation block: MYCN overexpression prevents Ascl1-driven differentiation, and loses that ability when Ascl1 cannot be phosphorylated.
edges.limitations: This is the differentiation-blocking arm of MYCN only. The node is about proliferation, and no proliferative or tumour-growth readout was taken here; MYCN is introduced by overexpression in a normal embryo, not by the genomic amplification that defines high-risk neuroblastoma.
edges.source: Xenopus anteroventral noradrenergic (AVNA) cell differentiation model

nodes.description: ALK tyrosine kinase inhibition targets the constitutive ALK signalling produced by activating ALK point mutations or ALK amplification. nodes.description: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT), the recombination-based telomere maintenance mechanism that works without telomerase. Its measured frequency depends on cohort and assay: C-circle screening classified 9.2% of a 720-tumour screening cohort as ALT-positive, ALT-associated PML nuclear bodies marked 49 of 273 pretreatment neuroblastomas, and the C-circle assay marked 25 of 107 high-risk tumours from patients older than 18 months. In a registry cohort of 40 relapsed tumours, 47.5% were ALT-positive. ATRX alterations are found in only about half to 60% of ALT tumours. In primary tumours, ALT and the routes to telomerase activation occur almost mutually exclusively, and ATRX mutation and MYCN amplification co-occurred in only 1 of 819 tumours. ALT-positive neuroblastomas proliferate slowly, with a protracted clinical course, yet children with these tumours have a dismal outcome. About a third of ALT-positive tumours present with localized disease classified as low or intermediate risk, and in one cohort survival did not differ between ALT-positive tumours classified high risk and those classified low or intermediate risk.

nodes.description: Reduced abundance of the ATRX/DAXX chromatin remodelling complex, a recurrent molecular feature of alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) in neuroblastoma. ATRX encodes an ATP-dependent helicase of the SWI/SNF family of chromatin remodellers and, with DAXX, deposits the histone variant H3.3 at telomeric regions. ALT-positive neuroblastomas show reduced ATRX/DAXX complex abundance, due either to ATRX mutation (55% of them in one cohort) or to low protein expression, while mutations in the complex members DAXX and H3F3A were extremely rare. In a pooled analysis of published ATRX-altered neuroblastomas, 68% of ATRX aberrations were multi-exon deletions, and 75% of these were predicted to be in-frame. ATRX mutation is strongly age-dependent: in 104 patients with metastatic disease, sampled to represent each age group, it was found in tumours from 14 of 32 adolescents and young adults, 9 of 54 children and none of 18 infants, although infant cases are reported. In the pooled analysis, each of the three types of ATRX aberration was more frequent in patients diagnosed at an older age, yet about 40% of the ATRX-aberrant patients were five years or younger at diagnosis.

nodes.description: Telomerase-mediated telomere maintenance, one of the two telomere maintenance mechanisms in neuroblastoma. TERT rearrangements at 5p15.33 juxtapose the TERT coding sequence to strong enhancer elements, with chromatin remodelling and DNA methylation of the affected region, and despite their structural diversity they all induced massive transcriptional upregulation of TERT. MYCN amplification raises TERT transcription, and some tumours have high TERT expression with neither alteration. In 457 pretreatment neuroblastomas, TERT rearrangement was found in 46 and MYCN amplification in 93, and high TERT expression without either in 10 of 223 tumours with expression data. TERT promoter mutations are rare: none was found in 131 primary tumours representing the whole spectrum of the disease, and a single-centre series found them in 17 of 603 tumours. Activated telomerase, defined by these routes, was associated with the poorest overall survival and was an independent prognostic marker in multivariable analyses. Enzymatic telomerase activity has been shown in neuroblastoma cell lines that carry a TERT rearrangement or MYCN amplification.

nodes.description: The ability of tumour cells to keep dividing indefinitely, which a telomere maintenance mechanism (telomerase activation or ALT) provides. Its binding, increased cell population proliferation, follows the module node it conforms to and means expansion continuing past the limit that telomere shortening sets on normal cells, not a faster division rate: ALT-positive neuroblastomas proliferate more slowly than telomerase-activated ones. Aggressive neuroblastomas show a prolonged evolution during which they acquire telomere maintenance mechanisms, whereas tumours with a favourable prognosis expand clonally after a short evolution. In pretreatment neuroblastomas, patients whose tumours lacked a telomere maintenance mechanism had an excellent prognosis and those whose tumours had one did substantially worse. Within high-risk disease the picture is less clear: in one cohort the telomere maintenance groups differed in overall but not in event-free survival, and a subset of high-risk tumours lacks significant telomere lengthening activity, with cells derived from them proliferating for more than 200 population doublings while their telomeres shortened.

nodes.description: Rather than growing a tumour, this model reconstructs the normal differentiation of the neural-crest-derived sympathoadrenal cell that neuroblastoma is thought to arise from, and asks what stops it. Frog AVNA cells differentiate under transient Ascl1 expression; in neuroblastoma cells Ascl1 is instead persistently expressed and multiply phosphorylated. Introducing that phospho-state into the frog cells blocks their differentiation, and CDK or MYCN overexpression blocks it too — but not when Ascl1 cannot be phosphorylated, which places phosphorylation downstream of both. The model tests the differentiation-arrest hypothesis in a normal developmental context; it does not produce tumours and so says nothing about transformation, growth, or metastasis.
